Pulmonology · published research

Lung inflammation

Across rodent models of LPS exposure, allergic inflammation, formaldehyde exposure, and ischemia-reperfusion, PBM often reduced inflammatory-cell influx, leakage, or selected cytokines. No human treatment outcome was identified in this category.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Across rodent models of LPS exposure, allergic inflammation, formaldehyde exposure, and ischemia-reperfusion, PBM often reduced inflammatory-cell influx, leakage, or selected cytokines. No human treatment outcome was identified in this category.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Respiratory system > Lung inflammation category contains 17 titles: 15 rodent experiments, seven in mice and eight in rats, plus two animal-focused meta-analyses. The syntheses reuse preclinical studies and do not add new experimental cohorts. No human treatment trial is listed for this indication.

Human and clinical evidence

No direct clinical PBM study for lung inflammation was identified in the assigned category. Human asthma, COPD, or pneumonia reports belong to neighboring indications and should not be counted as lung-inflammation trials.

Animal evidence

Experiments model allergic airway inflammation, bacterial lipopolysaccharide exposure, acute respiratory distress, formaldehyde exposure, and gut ischemia-reperfusion. Many report lower inflammatory-cell influx, pulmonary leakage, myeloperoxidase activity, or selected cytokines after light treatment. Results depend on the model and the measured endpoint; they do not establish a common treatment effect in patients. Aimbire et al. reported reduced airway hyperreactivity and neutrophil influx in an LPS-induced rat model (2005). Later animal meta-analyses summarize overlapping experiments and report changes in inflammatory markers (Raji et al. 2021 Arjmand and Rahim 2023).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo publication is listed in this category. Cell-associated measurements within animal studies are not separate laboratory cohorts.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Protocols use red or near-infrared light, including 685-nm laser in an LPS rat model, and vary in dose, timing, and delivery site. Wavelength names the light's color band and affects tissue penetration. Because experimental models and settings differ, there is no single lung-inflammation protocol to generalize.

Interpretation

The evidence supports preclinical effects on selected inflammatory measures. A human clinical effect has not been demonstrated in this indication. Animal replication should clarify dose-response and functional outcomes before patient trials are interpreted as disease treatment.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow-to-moderate for reducing selected inflammatory outcomes in defined rodent models No direct human treatment evidence identified

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Fifteen animal experiments and two animal-focused meta-analyses report changes in inflammatory cells, leakage, or cytokines, but models and light protocols vary. Human treatment evidence is absent in this category. Replication with standardized outcomes and transparent dose reporting is needed before testing clinical benefit.
